# Close task

> Closes a built task of a Gradatim project's open sprint, with each acceptance criterion shown, a code review to pick fixes from, and the documents it made stale brought in line. Use when the user asks for Gradatim's close task step, or to close, finish or wrap up a built task.

| | |
|---|---|
| Skill | `close-task`, [its file](../../skills/close-task/SKILL.md) |
| Step | 9 of 14: close task |
| Runs | After the task's build |
| Next | draft PR where a pull request is due; else design task for the next task, or close sprint when no task is left to do |
| Call it | `/gradatim:close-task` on Claude Code; [the other hosts](install.md#calling-a-skill) |

## When to use it

- The user asks for Gradatim's close task step, or to close, finish or wrap up a built task of the open sprint.
- Not for a task that isn't built, or whose build stopped: that is [`build-task`](build-task.md). Not for a new task, an urgent bug or work split off a task: that is [`new-sprint`](new-sprint.md)'s "add a task", which this step follows on its own for a criterion the user moves. Not for the pull request: that is [`draft-pr`](draft-pr.md). Not for the sprint's close: that is [`close-sprint`](close-sprint.md). Not for a change of the project's direction: that is [`decide-direction`](decide-direction.md), or [`write-architecture`](write-architecture.md) for the stack and the modules. Not for a folder with no Gradatim project: that is [`init-project`](init-project.md).

## What it reads and writes

| Document | Path | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Agent file | `AGENTS.md` | reads |
| Agent docs | `docs/agents/<topic>.md` | reads |
| Architecture | `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | reads |
| Sprint rules and index | `docs/sprints/README.md` | reads |
| Sprint README | `docs/sprints/sprint-<n>/README.md` | reads, changes |
| Task file | `docs/sprints/sprint-<n>/<ID>-<slug>.md` | reads, changes |
| Design | `docs/plans/<ID>-<slug>-design.md` | reads, changes |
| Issue | `docs/issues/YYYY-MM-DD-<ID>-<topic>.md` | reads |

It also reads the project's code and the task's diff. It writes the project's own files that the task made wrong or stale, outside the map, as documents.md's rule 4 says: its code, its tests, its README and a changelog. The map's other documents change only through [the sync](../../skills/method/references/sync.md) and [the change](../../skills/method/references/change.md), at the yes. Work split off goes through new sprint's "add a task", which writes the new task. It writes no issue, no deferred item and no `CLAUDE.md`.
